subject: AWS private offer: term-length options, finance sensitivity, and AWS checkpoint
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Alice Bowman <alice.bowman@amazon.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@helixlabs.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer: term-length options, finance sensitivity, and AWS checkpoint

Team / Priya —

Thanks for the productive call Friday. My note here to capture the action items and align on the private-offer framing we discussed so Helix can circulate to Finance. High-level ask from Helix: they need a clear pricing/term matrix that explains how annual commit vs monthly usage affects unit price and buyer approval flow. They also asked for a short justification memo that their procurement can attach to a PO.

Proposal (to confirm):
- Option A: 12-month annual commitment with 20% list discount; invoiced monthly; AWS private offer submitted under Helix account (lowest buyer friction).
- Option B: 24-month annual commitment with 28% discount + 1 month free; requires CFO approval and legal review (longer cycle).
- Option C: No-commit monthly usage at list with volume-based stepdowns (fastest to approve, higher unit cost).

Dependencies / gating items:
- Finance at Helix will require a template PO with the exact payment terms and a short note on data handling (we should include our SOC2 header).
- AWS (Alice) flagged a checkpoint review if we request a longer-than-12-month term with marketplace entitlements — we should make that explicit so Helix understands potential time impact.

Attachments: draft term sheet (helix_po_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a PO template (Helix_PO_Template.docx) included.

Next steps I propose: Lukas to share the draft term sheet (attached), Vanessa to draft the one-paragraph justification memo for procurement, Karthik to sanity-check pricing math and discount thresholds, Tessa to prepare the expected timeline (internal + AWS checkpoint). Priya / Jason — could you confirm which option (A/B/C) to prioritize and your target procurement date?

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Director, GTM — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: helix_po_term_sheet_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: Helix_PO_Template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixlabs.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Li <jason.li@helixlabs.com>, Alice Bowman <alice.bowman@amazon.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer: term-length options, finance sensitivity, and AWS checkpoint

Lukas —

Thanks, this is clear and helpful. Quick answers from procurement side:
- Our preferred path is Option A (12-month commit) because our finance team prefers annual visibility; Option B would be great if we can see a stronger uplift on the discount or additional co-sell credits.
- Target procurement date: hoping to have approvals by May 6, 2027 (EOD) so we can execute a PO and hit a June go-live.
- Key gating: our legal needs a one-page summary of data residency + retention; finance needs a line on refund/termination.

Two asks for Redwood: 1) can you call out the difference in effective $/token (or per-seat equivalent) between A and C in the term sheet, and 2) please indicate whether 24-month requests typically trigger the AWS checkpoint Alice mentioned and how much time that adds (estimate).

I'll loop in Jason to confirm internal approvers.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Procurement, Helix Labs

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixlabs.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Alice Bowman <alice.bowman@amazon.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer: term-length options, finance sensitivity, and AWS checkpoint

Priya / team —

Thanks for the preference. Per Lukas's note I updated the term sheet to include a short comparison table (effective unit price A vs C) and added the two bullets procurement requested (data residency + termination/refund language). I've left placeholders where legal needs to input exact retention windows.

Karthik — can you validate the numbers? I'm listing the effective cost as a blended token-equivalent; if you prefer a per-seat model I can add an alternate column.

Jason — for approvals, can you share the names/titles of the approvers and whether a CFO signature is required for >$200k spend? That will change the timeline.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer: term-length options, finance sensitivity, and AWS checkpoint

Quick pricing sanity check from me. I updated the term sheet (v1 -> v1.1) with the effective $/1k tokens equivalents and a second view that maps to a conservative "per-seat" monthly estimate for Helix's 150-seat pilot. Key notes:
- Option A (12mo, 20%): effective price ~ $0.048 / 1k token-equivalent (blended).
- Option B (24mo, 28% + 1mo free): effective price ~ $0.041 / 1k token-equivalent; marginally better but triggers additional paperwork.
- Option C (monthly): effective price ~ $0.062 / 1k token-equivalent initially, with stepdown bands at usage thresholds.

AWS checkpoint: Alice — from past experience the checkpoint for >12mo marketplaces typically adds 7-12 business days if there are entitlements that must be verified (co-sell credits, extended billing terms). If AWS routes to a partner approval path it can be longer. Recommend we call out an 8-10 business day buffer for planning.

I've attached the v1.1 file to this email and noted the cells where Finance will want hard numbers.

Karthik
Senior Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: helix_po_term_sheet_v1.1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alice Bowman <alice.bowman@amazon.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer: term-length options, finance sensitivity, and AWS checkpoint

Hi all —

Thanks for looping me in. Confirming AWS-side checkpoint expectations: when a seller requests private-offer terms beyond 12 months or includes marketplace entitlements (co-sell credits, advanced billing) we run a short review to validate the offer configuration and buyer eligibility. Typical cadence: 5-10 business days for standard checks + another possible 3-5 days if we need additional compliance confirmations. If Redwood provides an explicit justification and the buyer's procurement/legal attestation (one-pager) it helps shorten the cycle.

Action items for Helix to expedite:
- Attach the one-page data residency + retention summary (Vanessa / Lukas to provide).
- Confirm the approver list and whether consolidated CFO signoff will be needed for the expected spend.

If Helix targets May 6 for approvals, my recommendation is to aim to finalize the private-offer draft with Redwood by Apr 20 to allow time for the AWS checkpoint and any DocuSign execution. Happy to triage internally if we see a blocker.

Best,
Alice Bowman
AWS Marketplace — Partner Programs
